STEP 1 - Vessel type: The vessel has a clear curved inner wall rising from a flat base, with the food sitting low inside and a visible shadow along the back wall. This is a shallow bowl, or possibly a square plate with raised sides. I'll treat it as a shallow bowl with a square outline.

STEP 2 - Vessel size:
a) Type cue: a square serving bowl/plate of this look is typically 20-25 cm across.
b) Reference cue: the avocado wedge is about 10-11 cm long. Across the bowl's interior, the avocado and greens span roughly one-third to two-fifths of the width, and the bowl is roughly two avocado lengths across, so about 20-22 cm.
Reconciled width: about 21 cm.

STEP 3 - Food items:
- Avocado: two wedges, one standing and one lying flat. Roughly 2 wedges of ~40 g each of flesh, so about 60 g in total (the standing wedge is thick, the flat one thinner).
- Cooked chard/leafy greens with red stems: a loose mound covering about 25% of the bowl floor. Footprint ≈ 0.25 × 21² ≈ 110 cm². Average thickness of a loose mound ≈ 2.5 cm, so volume ≈ 275 ml. Cooked greens at 0.6 g/ml gives about 165 g. Some of it is stems, which are denser, so I take about 150 g.
- Red chard stems (separate pieces, visible among the greens): included in the greens above, so no separate item.

STEP 4 - Hidden food: no base layer is visible under the items; the bowl floor is visible and largely empty, so nothing is hidden.

STEP 5 - kcal per 100 g (as served):
- Avocado: ~160 kcal/100 g.
- Cooked chard: ~20 kcal/100 g (chard is low in energy; a light oil or dressing is not visible).

Totals: avocado ≈ 60 g (≈ 96 kcal); cooked greens ≈ 150 g (≈ 30 kcal). Total ≈ 210 g, ≈ 126 kcal.
